sections.h2: Who sets and collects property tax in Ocean County, NJ?
sections.html:
In Ocean County the town assessor sets the value of a house and the town tax collector sends the bill. The county itself runs the Ocean County Board of Taxation, which hears assessment disputes. The board's own contact page says property tax inquiries go to the tax collector of the municipality where the home sits.

The county has 33 municipalities, from Lakewood and Toms River to small shore boroughs such as Harvey Cedars and Mantoloking. Each one bills on its own schedule inside the state framework, so the first call for any Ocean County seller is the collector in the town that holds the parcel.

  • Ocean County Board of Taxation: Ocean County Court House, Room 215, 118 Washington Street, Toms River, phone (732) 929-2008.
  • Town assessor: value, deductions and exemption forms.
  • Town tax collector: balances, payoff figures and payment options.
  • County Clerk: recording of the deed after a sale.

sections.h2: What should a seller know about the Ocean County housing market's tax backdrop?
sections.html:
Ocean County is the fastest-growing county in New Jersey since 2020, with a 2025 Census estimate of 673,746 residents, up 5.7% from the 2020 base. It sits about 70 miles south of New York City and 25 miles north of Atlantic City, and more than 31% of its total area is water, mostly Barnegat Bay and the Atlantic coast.

Census QuickFacts for 2020 to 2024 shows owners in 80.7% of housing units, a median owner-occupied value of $398,400 and a median household income of $89,863. People 65 and older make up 24.0% of the population, a share that matters because several state relief programs are aimed at older owners. Ocean County issued 2,831 building permits in 2025.

Growth spread unevenly. Lakewood Township had an estimated 139,866 residents in 2023, while Jackson Township covers 100.62 square miles, the largest area of any town. A bayfront bungalow in Brick, a retirement-community home in Manchester and a Lakewood multifamily house can carry very different assessments and very different bills.

sections.h2: When are Ocean County property tax bills due, and what does late payment cost?
sections.html:
New Jersey property tax is paid in quarterly installments due February 1, May 1, August 1 and November 1. Each municipality may fix interest on late payments by resolution, capped at 8% a year on the first $1,500 of the delinquency and 18% a year above that, counted from the due date.

A town can also allow a ten day grace period before interest starts. Whether a given Ocean County town does so is a local resolution, so ask that town's collector before relying on a grace window. A delinquency over $10,000 can also draw a year-end penalty of up to 6% where the town has adopted one (R.S. 54:4-67).

Unpaid balances can end up in a tax sale. Under R.S. 54:5-19, a town may run an accelerated sale for amounts still unpaid on the 11th day of the eleventh month of the fiscal year. A seller who is behind should get a written payoff before listing, because the lien stays with the parcel and comes out of the sale proceeds at closing.

sections.h2: How do I appeal an assessment to the Ocean County Board of Taxation?
sections.html:
File a petition of appeal with the Ocean County Board of Taxation by April 1 of the tax year, or by May 1 if your town did a municipal wide revaluation or reassessment. If assessment notices were mailed late, the deadline is 45 days after the bulk mailing. The board must receive the petition, not just have it postmarked, by 4:30 p.m. on the last day.

  • File one petition per parcel and serve a copy on the town assessor and the municipal clerk.
  • Pay the filing fee by check to the Ocean County Treasurer: $5 under $150,000 of assessed value, $25 from $150,000 to under $500,000, $100 from $500,000 to under $1,000,000, and $150 at $1,000,000 or more.
  • Send comparable sales (no more than five) and any appraisal at least seven days before the hearing.
  • Be current on all taxes through the first quarter of the tax year, as N.J.S.A. 54:3-27 requires.

The appeal covers the assessed value only, not the tax bill, and the assessment is presumed correct. Hearings usually start at 9:00 a.m. Skipping a hearing without written notice of postponement leads to dismissal for lack of prosecution, which cannot go to Tax Court. A county board judgment can be taken to the Tax Court of New Jersey within 45 days of mailing, and if no further appeal is filed the judgment generally holds for the next two years under the freeze provision.

sections.h2: What are the Chapter 123 ratios in Ocean County?
sections.html:
Chapter 123 compares your assessment with the true value of the home using a town's average ratio. If your ratio lands outside the 15% common level range around that average, the board resets the assessment. The table shows the tax year 2025 figures the county board published for five towns.

sections.h2: Which tax relief programs can Ocean County owners use?
sections.html:
The state's Division of Taxation runs Senior Freeze, ANCHOR and Stay NJ through one combined application, and the Fiscal Year 2027 budget funds all three. The deadline for the 2025 application was November 2, 2026, so that window has closed; check the Division's page for the next filing period.

  • Senior Freeze reimburses eligible seniors and disabled owners for increases in property tax on a main home.
  • ANCHOR gives relief to owners and renters who live in the property as their main home and meet income limits.
  • Local deductions for veterans, seniors and disabled owners come through the town assessor, and a dispute over a denied deduction can be filed with the county board at no fee.

With 24.0% of Ocean County residents at 65 or older, many sellers here have these benefits attached to the home, so tell the buyer's side which ones end at sale.

sections.h2: What does selling a house in Ocean County involve at the county level?
sections.html:
The deed is recorded at the Ocean County Clerk's Office. The county's published schedule lists a deed at $45 for the first page and $10 for each added page, a mortgage at $35 first page, and a $20 surcharge when a document comes without a recording cover sheet. Payment is by cash, check or escrow account, and checks over $10,000 must be certified.

Before closing, ask the town collector for a tax search and a payoff letter, and ask the assessor whether a pending appeal, added assessment or deduction affects the next bill. Old tax sale certificates are recorded at the Clerk's Office as well, at $35, and must be redeemed or cancelled for clean title.

faqs.q: Where do I pay Ocean County property tax?
faqs.a: You pay the tax collector of your own municipality, not the county. The Ocean County Board of Taxation says property tax inquiries belong with the collector in the town where the property is located.

faqs.q: What is the Ocean County appeal deadline?
faqs.a: April 1 of the tax year, or May 1 where the town completed a revaluation or reassessment, or 45 days after bulk mailing of notices if that is later. The petition must be received by 4:30 p.m. on the last day, and a weekend or holiday deadline moves to the next business day.

faqs.q: Can I appeal my tax bill in Ocean County?
faqs.a: No. Only the assessed value can be appealed, because taxes come from the budget process. You must show the market value as of the preceding October 1 with sales or an appraisal, and you must overcome the presumption that the assessment is correct.

faqs.q: How much does it cost to file a tax appeal in Ocean County?
faqs.a: The fee runs from $5 to $150 by assessed value, paid by check to the Ocean County Treasurer. There is no fee to contest the denial of a veteran, senior or disabled deduction.

faqs.q: Can I sell my Ocean County house if I owe back property tax?
faqs.a: Yes. The balance and interest are paid from the proceeds at closing, so request a payoff figure from the town collector first. If a tax sale certificate has been issued, it must be redeemed before the title is clear.
